## 1. Summary

- **PRIMARY result (official `eval_depth.py`):** over all {{all_frames_scored}} test frames, AbsRel {{all_AbsRel}}, d1 {{all_d1}}, RMSE {{all_RMSE}} m (frame-weighted pooled row, ours). Per-subset AbsRel ranges from {{subset_absrel_min}} to {{subset_absrel_max}} (`{{subset_absrel_max_name}}`). No frame failed or was unscorable.
- **The dominant error is metric scale, and it is depth-dependent.** The per-frame ratio median(GT)/median(pred) is above 1 on {{scale_frac_gt1}}% of frames (median {{scale_median}}, 10th-90th percentile {{scale_p10}}-{{scale_p90}}). Pooled over pixels, median pred/GT falls monotonically from {{bin_first_ratio}} for GT in {{bin_first}} m to {{bin_last_ratio}} for GT in {{bin_last}} m: near content is roughly right, far content is strongly range-compressed.
- **Relative structure is much better than metric scale:** per-frame median alignment lowers mean AbsRel from {{all_AbsRel}} to {{medar_all}}. The per-frame scale ratio correlates with scene depth (Spearman rho = {{spearman_all}} vs. per-frame median GT depth).
- **The model's depth cap costs little in relative metrics.** At fx = 320 the pipeline cannot output more than {{cap}} m; {{frac_above_cap_all}}% of valid pixels lie beyond it. Excluding them changes AbsRel by {{d_absrel_all}} and d1 by {{d_d1_all}}, but RMSE by {{d_rmse_all}} m.
- **Field of view explains only part of the scale error.** Narrowing the FoV from 90° to {{fov_c2_deg}}° (centre crop, correct intrinsics) lowers the median scale ratio from {{fov_c0_med}} to {{fov_c2_med}}; against a resize-only control with the same resampling path it lowers the ratio by a factor {{pair_c2c3_factor}} ({{pair_c2c3_frac}}% of frames move closer to 1). Even at {{fov_c2_deg}}° most of the bias remains ({{fov_c2_log_remaining_pct}}% of C0's median log-ratio), so it is mainly content/domain (far-range compression), not FoV alone.
- **Scene type matters far more than subset, difficulty or pose.** Environment means range from AbsRel {{env_range}}; indoor scenes score best and large outdoor scenes worst. Easy vs. hard, camera face, pitch and dark frames change AbsRel little; roll shows a modest increase. Environment explains a much larger share of per-frame AbsRel variance (eta squared {{eta_env}}) than any other grouping (at most {{eta_other_max}}).
- **Correctness:** our wrapper reproduces the official Metric3D test pipeline bit for bit (max abs difference {{eq_kitti_dmax}} on KITTI and {{eq_nyu_dmax}} on NYU demo frames, depth and normals); predictions and metrics were re-checked across runs (exact matches).

## 2. Setup

**Model.** Metric3D v2-S: DINOv2-reg ViT-Small encoder + RAFT-style GRU decoder ({{raft_iters}} iterations) predicting depth and surface normals. Config `{{config}}` (unchanged: input `crop_size` {{crop_h}}x{{crop_w}}, canonical focal length {{canon_focal}}, decoder depth clamp [{{clamp_min}}, {{clamp_max}}] in canonical space). Weights `{{weights_path}}` (the official `metric_depth_vit_small_800k.pth`), sha256 `{{weights_sha256}}`.

**Inference pipeline (official, unmodified).** We call the repo's own `mono/utils/do_test.py` functions (`transform_test_data_scalecano`, `get_prediction`) and replicate the math of `postprocess_per_image` exactly; model building and checkpoint loading mirror `mono/tools/test_scale_cano.py` (DataParallel + `load_ckpt`). Per frame:

1. **Canonical camera transform.** The image is treated as if taken by a camera with focal length {{canon_focal}}: depth labels scale by {{canon_focal}} / f. The {{src_side}}x{{src_side}} image is resized to {{resize_side}}x{{resize_side}} and padded with the ImageNet mean by {{pad_desc}} to {{crop_h}}x{{crop_w}}. The combined **label scale factor** is ({{canon_focal}} / {{fx}}) x ({{src_side}} / {{resize_side}}) = **{{lsf}}** (`{{lsf_full}}`).
2. **Forward pass.** The network predicts canonical depth, clamped to [{{clamp_min}}, {{clamp_max}}].
3. **Back to metric.** Remove the padding, bilinearly resize to {{src_side}}x{{src_side}}, divide by the label scale factor, zero anything outside (0, 300) m.

**The network never sees the intrinsics.** In this code path `cam_model` is passed as `None` and is unused by the model (in both the inference and training trees); intrinsics only enter through the label scale factor in steps 1 and 3. The network must therefore infer canonical depth from the apparent size of things in pixels.

**Test set.** TartanAir v2 test package: {{frames_total}} frames, {{n_subsets}} mutually exclusive subsets, {{n_envs}} environments, 640x640 RGB, planar-Z depth in metres, official valid mask (depth in (0.001, 200] m and not sky). Every frame has the same pinhole intrinsics ({{intr_desc}}; 90° FoV).

{{TABLE:subset_sizes}}

Hardware: {{gpu}}. Full-set inference took {{infer_s}} s ({{infer_min}} min; {{sec_per_frame}} s per frame including zip read and save, {{infer_per_frame}} s model time), batch size 1.

## 3. Correctness checks

1. **Wrapper vs. official inference.** `tartanair_eval/check_equivalence.py` runs the unmodified official `do_scalecano_test_with_custom_data` on the repo's demo annotations and captures its final post-processed depth and normals by wrapping (not editing) three functions at runtime, then runs our wrapper on the same images and intrinsics. Max abs difference: KITTI ({{eq_kitti_n}} frames) depth {{eq_kitti_dmax}}, normals {{eq_kitti_nmax}}; NYU ({{eq_nyu_n}} frames) depth {{eq_nyu_dmax}}, normals {{eq_nyu_nmax}}.
2. **Official smoke test on KITTI / NYU demos.** This repo version computes but never prints its metrics (the print block is behind `if False:`), so we read them from the official metric meters via the same harness. They are plausible for a metric-depth model on these demos. The repo's meter reports SILog as a fraction (not x100 as in `eval_depth.py`), and its NYU global-aligned SILog/d2 values are invalid (NaN, > 1) and should be ignored.

## 4. Evaluation protocol

**PRIMARY (the number to report and compare).** The dataset's `metrics/eval_depth.py`, unmodified, run with `python -B` on predictions saved as float32 640x640 metres. It scores each frame on its own valid mask and averages per subset with equal weight per frame (AbsRel, SqRel, RMSE, RMSElog, log10, SILog, d1-d3, MAE). The script reports per subset only; the **all frames** row is our frame-weighted mean over all scored frames, computed from its per-frame output.

**DIAGNOSTIC (ours; explains the PRIMARY numbers, never replaces them).** All use `eval_depth.py`'s own functions imported by path:
- *Capped mask:* official valid mask AND GT <= cap, to measure what the model's maximum depth costs.
- *Scale ratio:* per frame, median(GT) / median(pred) on the official valid mask (> 1 = prediction too small).
- *Median-aligned AbsRel:* AbsRel after multiplying the prediction by that per-frame ratio (scale-free relative accuracy).

**How the {{cap}} m cap follows from the code.** The decoder clamps canonical depth at {{clamp_max}} (`depth_normalize` / `max_value` in the config). Metric depth = canonical depth / label scale factor, so the largest metric depth the pipeline can output at fx = 320, 640x640 is {{clamp_max}} / {{lsf}} = **{{cap}} m** (and the smallest is {{cap_min}} m). The cap depends on the intrinsics and image size (e.g. KITTI's demo frames saturate at {{kitti_pred_max}} m).

## 6. Error analysis (DIAGNOSTIC)

### 6.1 Scale ratio vs. scene depth

![scale ratio histograms]({{fig_scale_ratio_hist}})

![scale ratio vs median GT depth]({{fig_scale_vs_median_gt}})

The per-frame scale ratio grows with the frame's median GT depth (Spearman rho = {{spearman_all}} over all frames). Frames whose median depth is a metre or two have ratios close to 1; frames dominated by tens of metres are under-predicted several-fold.

![median pred/GT vs depth]({{fig_depth_bin_ratio}})

{{share_under_5}}% of valid pixels are within 5 m; there the median pred/GT is {{bin_first_ratio}} (0-2 m) and {{bin_2_5_ratio}} (2-5 m). It then falls to {{bin_5_10_ratio}} (5-10 m), {{bin_10_20_ratio}} (10-20 m) and down to {{bin_last_ratio}} (100-200 m): predictions are range-compressed, increasingly with distance. Bins beyond {{cap}} m are additionally limited by the cap. (Bin medians come from a log-ratio histogram with {{ratio_hist_res}}% resolution.)

### 6.5 Field-of-view experiment

**Question.** Does a narrower field of view bring the scale ratio closer to 1? If so, the scale error is mainly a FoV / apparent-size effect; if not, it is content or domain.

**Design.** {{fov_n}} frames (50 per subset, seeded, {{fov_envs}} environments). Four conditions, each through the same wrapper with correctly adjusted intrinsics:

- **C0 full**: 640x640, fx = fy = 320, 90° FoV (equals the Stage-2 prediction).
- **C1 crop448**: centre crop 448x448, cx = cy = 224, about {{fov_c1_deg}}°.
- **C2 crop320**: centre crop 320x320, cx = cy = 160, about {{fov_c2_deg}}°.
- **C3 resize320** (control): the full image resized to 320x320 (INTER_AREA), fx = fy = 160. Same 90° FoV as C0, but the same down- then up-sampling path as C2. C2 vs. C3 therefore isolates the FoV from resolution and blur.

All conditions are scored on the same pixels: the central 320x320 region of the official valid mask (C0/C1 predictions cropped; C3 prediction upsampled to 640 then cropped). Each condition has its own depth cap because the label scale factor changes with crop size.

{{TABLE:fov}}

Same, restricted to GT <= {{cap}} m (removes the effect of the different caps):

{{TABLE:fov_capped}}

Paired comparisons on the same frames (median ratio factor A/B < 1 means the scale ratio got smaller in A, i.e. A's prediction is larger; since most ratios are above 1 this usually means closer to the GT scale, which the 'closer to 1' column counts directly; CI by bootstrap over frames):

{{TABLE:fov_paired}}

Per-subset median scale ratio:

{{TABLE:fov_subset}}

![FoV ratio distribution]({{fig_fov_ratio_distribution}})

![FoV examples]({{fig_fov_examples}})

**Answer: partially.** Narrowing the FoV moves the ratio toward 1 consistently (C1 and C2 vs. C0: factors {{pair_c1c0_factor}} and {{pair_c2c0_factor}}; {{pair_c1c0_frac}}% / {{pair_c2c0_frac}}% of frames closer to 1; 95% CIs exclude zero). Against the resolution-matched control the FoV effect is larger (C2 vs. C3: factor {{pair_c2c3_factor}}, {{pair_c2c3_frac}}% of frames closer), because the down/up-sampling path on its own makes the ratio worse (C3 vs. C0: factor {{pair_c3c0_factor}}). The capped variant gives the same picture, so the per-condition cap is not the driver. But even at {{fov_c2_deg}}° the median ratio is still {{fov_c2_med}}, so the FoV accounts for a minority of the bias; most of it is the depth-dependent range compression seen in 6.1-6.2, i.e. content/domain. Mean AbsRel improves only slightly (C0 {{fov_c0_absrel}}, C2 {{fov_c2_absrel}}), and the effect is not uniform across subsets (e.g. `test_scene` does not improve).

## 8. Implications for fine-tuning (observations, not decisions)

- **Scale bias.** Zero-shot v2-S under-predicts TartanAir depth (median scale ratio {{scale_median}}), and the bias grows with distance (median pred/GT {{bin_first_ratio}} at {{bin_first}} m to {{bin_last_ratio}} at {{bin_last}} m). Fine-tuning has to correct a depth-dependent range compression, not just a single global scale factor.
- **Canonical clamp.** Under the same canonical transform as at inference (f = 320 -> 1000, 640 -> 616), canonical depth = GT x {{canon_mult}}. With the decoder clamp at {{clamp_max}}, GT beyond {{cap}} m ({{frac_above_cap_all}}% of valid test pixels; the valid mask itself reaches 200 m) would be clipped in training as well, unless `depth_normalize` / `max_value` is raised or the training resize changes the factor.
- **Padding.** Square 640x640 frames resized to {{resize_side}}x{{resize_side}} and padded into the {{crop_h}}x{{crop_w}} input leave {{wasted_pct}}% of the input as padding. A square or differently shaped training crop could use that compute for image content.
- **Will the subsets discriminate?** Zero-shot, the subsets differ little relative to the environment spread: per-subset AbsRel {{subset_absrel_min}}-{{subset_absrel_max}}; `test_scene` (unseen environments; the largest share of valid pixels beyond the cap, {{ts_frac_above_cap}}% vs. at most {{other_frac_above_cap_max}}% elsewhere) separates clearly, and `pose_extrapolation` sits above `test_matched` ({{ci_overlap_note}}). The bootstrap CIs below resample frames and ignore correlation within trajectories and environments, so they are optimistic. Whether the pose/height subsets separate after fine-tuning cannot be judged from zero-shot results; with the domain gap removed, the pose and height effects may become more visible, or remain small.

{{TABLE:subset_ci}}

## 9. Limitations and open questions

- Zero-shot v2-S only; larger v2 models (L, giant2) were not evaluated.
- DIAGNOSTIC analyses are ours. Bootstrap CIs treat frames as independent, which they are not (shared trajectories and environments).
- The FoV experiment uses {{fov_n}} frames and compares central crops; cropping changes image content as well as FoV, and the depth cap differs per condition (the capped variant controls for the latter).
- Brightness and roll effects are correlational and may be confounded with scene type.
- Some GT depth maps contain rendered weather particles (e.g. falling snow in `MiddleEast`) inside the valid mask (visible in the FoV examples); we did not quantify how often this happens.
- Pixel-bin medians come from a histogram ({{ratio_hist_res}}% resolution).
- Not verified: the sha256 of the seven test zips (only `frames.tsv` and `eval_depth.py` were checked against the dataset README).
- Open: why the model compresses far range on TartanAir; how much is synthetic-domain appearance vs. the 90° FoV vs. scene layout (the FoV experiment bounds the FoV share only for central crops).

## 10. Reproduction

Base upstream commit `{{base_commit}}` (`ORIGINAL_COMMIT.txt`); work on branch `gilbreth-run`. Environment and node rules are in the repo's `CLAUDE.md`. Outputs live under `{{out_root}}` (scratch).

```bash
cd ~/MMDE/metric3d-v2
OUT={{out_root}}; F=$OUT/full; S3=$OUT/stage3; T=/depot/chan129/data/TartanAir_v2/tartanair_v2_test
# Stage 1: official smoke test, equivalence, pilot
python -B mono/tools/test_scale_cano.py {{config}} --load-from {{weights_path}} \
    --test_data_path ./data/kitti_demo/test_annotations.json --launcher None --show-dir $OUT/stage1/smoke/kitti
python -B tartanair_eval/check_equivalence.py --annos data/kitti_demo/test_annotations.json \
    --show-dir $OUT/stage1/equiv/kitti_official --out $OUT/stage1/equiv/kitti_equivalence.json    # same for nyu
python -B tartanair_eval/select_keys.py --per-subset 3 --out $OUT/stage1/pilot/pilot_keys.txt
python -B tartanair_eval/infer_tartanair.py --keys-file $OUT/stage1/pilot/pilot_keys.txt --out-dir $OUT/stage1/pilot
python -B tartanair_eval/score_pilot.py --keys-file $OUT/stage1/pilot/pilot_keys.txt --run-dir $OUT/stage1/pilot
# Stage 2: full inference, PRIMARY and DIAGNOSTIC metrics, visuals
python -B tartanair_eval/infer_tartanair.py --out-dir $F --skip-existing --no-normals
python -B $T/metrics/eval_depth.py --data $T --pred $F/pred --out $F/eval_official --per-frame
python -B tartanair_eval/eval_capped.py --pred $F/pred --out $F/eval_capped --official-dir $F/eval_official
python -B tartanair_eval/select_keys.py --per-subset 4 --seed 0 --out $F/vis_frames_keys.txt
python -B tartanair_eval/infer_tartanair.py --keys-file $F/vis_frames_keys.txt --out-dir $F/vis_frames
python -B tartanair_eval/score_pilot.py --keys-file $F/vis_frames_keys.txt --run-dir $F/vis_frames --vis-dir $F/vis
# Stage 3: analysis, FoV experiment, extremes, report
python -B tartanair_eval/analyze_full.py --run-dir $F --out $S3/analysis --extremes-out $S3/extremes_keys.txt
python -B tartanair_eval/select_keys.py --per-subset 50 --seed 1 --out $S3/fov/fov_keys.txt
python -B tartanair_eval/fov_experiment.py --keys-file $S3/fov/fov_keys.txt --run-dir $F --out $S3/fov --fig $S3/vis/fov_examples.png
python -B tartanair_eval/infer_tartanair.py --keys-file $S3/extremes_keys.txt --out-dir $S3/vis_frames
python -B tartanair_eval/score_pilot.py --keys-file $S3/extremes_keys.txt --run-dir $S3/vis_frames --vis-dir $S3/vis --sheet-prefix sheet_extremes_
python -B tartanair_eval/build_report.py
```
